To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HNE metabolism is dependent on the availability of NAD+ in brain mitochondria, which is in turn dependent on the NADH/NDA(+) ratio, and that HNE metabolism decreases with age.
HNE metabolism by brain mitochondria is dependent upon the NAD+/NADH ratio and that HNE oxidation to HNEAcid is dependent upon complex I activity.
HNE metabolism by rat brain mitochondria is dependent upon age and NAD availability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mitochondria in the detoxification and metabolism of HNE, an important neurotoxic product formed during oxidative damage to lipids.
the metabolism and detoxification of HONE by mitochondria.
the metabolism of HNE in the CNS and how this process is altered in aging and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HNE oxidation is a saturable process with a K(M)(app) of 25 +/- 6 microM and a V(Max)(app) of approximately 4.5 nmol/min/mag of protein.
the mitochondrial metabolism of HNE to HNEAcid occurs via an NAD(+) dependent mechanism that is inhibited by complex I activity and that this metabolism is decreased with age.
the rate of mitochondrial HNE detoxification is age and NAD(+) dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mitochondrial metabolism of HNE to HNEAcid is dependent on NAD(+) and the activity of the respiratory chain.
HNE metabolism by mitochondria is dependent upon age, NAD(+) status, and the respiratory state.
the ability of mitochondria to detoxify HNE is dependent on age, NAD(+) concentration, and complex I activity and is a critical determinant of HNE toxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondrial matrix is the primary site of HNE metabolism in brain and that the availability of NAD(+) and the activity of complex I are critical factors in regulating HNE metabolism.
mitochondria are a major sink for HNE in the brain and that mitochondrial NAD(+) levels and complex I activity are important regulators of aldehyde detoxification in this organelle.
mitochondrial aldehyde detoxication is a critical component of the mitochondrial antioxidant defense system and is dependent on NAD(+) levels and complex I activity.
